title: Partial Audit Rules for Recovering Endpoint Intervention Distributions under Monotone Dropout
banked_reason: The promised arbitrary-local-graph necessary-and-sufficient audit criterion and full design frontier are replaced by an iff only for the at-most-one-informative-hazard subclass; the core itself leaves interacting hazards unresolved.
gap_reasons: The promised arbitrary-local-graph necessary-and-sufficient audit criterion and full design frontier are replaced by an iff only for the at-most-one-informative-hazard subclass; the core itself leaves interacting hazards unresolved.
The delivered necessary-and-sufficient criterion applies only when every hazard except one has no substantive parents; for arbitrary local graphs the note proves only a one-way obstruction.
The proof handles cancellation of one selection factor but does not resolve interacting hazards, overlapping-parent constraints, alphabet-sensitive bridges, or endpoint-only cancellations.
proof_attempt_summary: Three D0 solve rounds produced an explicit rational recovery, positive witness, exact minimal-design frontier, and regular plug-in inference for the sound at-most-one-informative-hazard subclass. The field-level claim collapsed because those arguments cancel only one selection factor and do not compose for arbitrary interacting local hazards. A future re-raise must supply the interval-state reconstruction and matching positive countermodel compiler for overlapping and alphabet-sensitive multi-hazard cases, including all positive rank strata.
tldr: For the arbitrary-horizon local subclass with at most one substantively informative continuation hazard, a finite graph-and-audit rule is necessary and sufficient for the entire endpoint intervention distribution. Empty or purely lagged hazard parents need no audit; current or lead parents require one pre-\(k\) dropout stratum to audit a coordinate at or downstream of the latest such parent. Successful passive and active branches return explicit rational reconstructions valid without rank assumptions, while failure returns a strictly positive observationally equivalent pair. The minimal frontier is the empty design in the passive case and otherwise consists of \(k(T-j_\star+1)\) singleton audits. A one-way embedded-witness obstruction applies to arbitrary local supergraphs, but sufficiency with two or more informative hazards remains open.
gap: Passive monotone-MNAR theory supplies local recovery operations and a self-censoring-path obstruction, while randomized double-sampling theory assumes that phase two completes the missing record. Neither decides endpoint identification when each dropout stratum reveals only a fixed subset of future coordinates.
fill: A constructive recovery-or-positive-obstruction calculus yields the exact graph-and-pattern criterion, an evaluable reconstruction, and every inclusion-minimal sufficient bundle design for arbitrary horizon.
